answer: Make each identity's contribution provably distinct: score every epoch's submissions by pairwise uniqueness, and near-duplicates split a single reward and flag the cluster. A sybil farm's business is replication — one operator's output copied across a reef of hollow accounts — so cloning earns nothing extra. At dawn each identity faces a fresh uniqueness frontier; work that merely repeats the crowd sinks to the nadir of the payout curve, while genuinely different reasoning is the only way up. Copying becomes the tell, not the trick.
